title: Transfer: waves and signals
target: Choose appropriate wave models and explain what a signal establishes.
criteria: Use wave speed and round-trip geometry correctly.
Separate frequency, amplitude and direction effects.
State the limits of an inference from a signal.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A simulated wave has frequency 8 Hz and wavelength 1.5 m. An echo takes 7 s. What is range in this scaled model?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A sensor is 30 m from a reflector. A pulse speed is 15 m/s in a scaled model. What echo delay should be used?
cpa.guide: The path is 60 m out and back; t = 60/15 = 4 s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two stationary speakers emit the same frequency in the same air, but one has greater amplitude. What does that difference mainly affect?
cpa.guide: Amplitude and frequency are separate; greater amplitude generally increases sound intensity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A light ray refracts obliquely into an ordinary slower medium at a stationary boundary. Which combination is expected?
options: Toward the normal; same wavelength and lower frequency.
No direction change is possible at any angle.
Toward the normal; lower speed and wavelength; same frequency.
Away from the normal; higher frequency.
cpa.guide: Speed changes, frequency remains continuous, and wavelength follows v/f; ordinary slower refraction bends toward normal.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A radar gives one range and one radial velocity measurement. Which conclusion goes beyond this evidence?
options: The exact full three-dimensional future path is known.
More observations could improve a path estimate.
Doppler shift constrains radial relative velocity.
cpa.guide: One radial component and range do not uniquely determine the full state or future forces.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Two thermal objects have the same peak wavelength in an ideal blackbody model. What is justified, and what is not determined by that peak alone?
options: Same model temperature; their total emitted powers need not match.
One must have zero visible emission.
Same total power and size are guaranteed.
cpa.guide: Wien’s law constrains temperature; total power also depends on emitting area and other assumptions.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
